statement: grill-with-docs is a workflow that sharpens a plan or design through interview while producing durable design docs (ADRs, glossary) as a side effect.

source.quote: description: A relentless interview to sharpen a plan or design, which also creates docs (ADR's and glossary) as we go.

trigger: user invokes grill-with-docs (or its trigger phrase) on a plan/design
outcome: the plan/design reaches shared understanding and ADR/glossary docs exist for the decisions made
notes: Old mechanism is a Claude-Code-specific skill file; the durable behavior is 'interview-driven design sharpening with document capture', independent of which harness runs it.
rationale: Has a recognizable trigger (grill-with-docs invocation), bounded outcome (shared understanding + docs), and completion condition — fits the reusable-procedural-outcome test (proposal 6.2).
alternatives_considered: actor stage of the grilling workflow (rejected: it is invoked as its own named skill with a distinct outcome — doc production — not merely one stage of grilling)

statement: grill-with-docs must be invoked explicitly by the user or another procedure; the assistant must not decide on its own to start it.

source.quote: disable-model-invocation: true

trigger: n/a — this is a standing constraint on when the workflow may start
outcome: the workflow never begins without an explicit invocation
notes: Mirrors the same field in triage/SKILL.md (BU citing that file) and the paired openai.yaml policy.allow_implicit_invocation:false — a repeated cross-skill convention for consent-gated or disruptive procedures.
rationale: Not a checkpoint inside one procedure; it is a reused invocation-gating convention that shows up wherever a skill should not silently self-trigger. Local to two skills observed in this partition (grill-with-docs, triage) so treated as a reused convention worth a shared entry, not baked into either workflow alone.
alternatives_considered: workflow-local metadata on grill-with-docs only
project-wide invariant (rejected: only applies to specific consent-gated skills, not universally)

statement: grill-with-docs is defined by composing two other procedures: it runs the grilling interview loop while using the domain-modeling skill to capture ADRs/glossary entries as decisions land.

source.quote: Run a `/grilling` session, using the `/domain-modeling` skill.

trigger: grill-with-docs invocation
outcome: a grilling interview occurs and its outputs are captured via domain-modeling's document conventions
notes: This is procedure-by-reference, not new procedure text — the whole 'workflow' is a pointer composing two others. The proposal's Phase A engine (7.7) does not yet support true nested workflow invocation as a runtime feature, but expressing 'run this other skill's guidance inline' as stage instruction text is already achievable by an actor stage today, so no engine capability is missing to represent this.
rationale: Defines the whole workflow's procedure as literally 'invoke grilling, then use domain-modeling' — the composition itself is the workflow content.
alternatives_considered: engine-gap: nested/composed workflow invocation as a first-class runtime primitive (considered and rejected — expressible today as actor-stage prose per proposal 9.2's actor-stage model; no durable fact the runtime itself must own to represent 'this actor should also apply that other skill's guidance')

statement: Cross-harness metadata mirrors the Claude-Code-specific disable-model-invocation flag so a non-Claude-Code harness (OpenCode) enforces the same explicit-invocation-only rule.

source.quote: allow_implicit_invocation: false

trigger: n/a — standing constraint
outcome: every harness that reads this metadata refuses to auto-trigger the skill
notes: Confirms the disable-model-invocation convention is meant to be harness-independent, not a Claude-Code-only quirk — two parallel declarations of the same policy in two metadata formats.
rationale: Deterministic mirrored metadata, not a checkpoint; belongs with the disable-model-invocation entry as one reused convention.
alternatives_considered: separate per-harness policies (rejected: the two files agree, indicating one intended cross-harness rule)

statement: grilling is a workflow that interviews the user to stress-test a plan, decision, or idea, triggered by an explicit request or grill trigger phrases.

source.quote: description: Grill the user relentlessly about a plan, decision, or idea. Use when the user wants to stress-test their thinking, or uses any 'grill' trigger phrases.

trigger: user asks to stress-test thinking, or uses a grill trigger phrase
outcome: shared understanding of the plan/decision/idea is reached
rationale: Recognizable trigger (grill phrases), bounded outcome (shared understanding), completion condition (explicit confirmation, see later BU) — a reusable procedural outcome.
alternatives_considered: stage of some larger review workflow (rejected: it is independently invocable by trigger phrase, not subordinate to another procedure)

statement: The interview proceeds systematically down a decision tree, resolving dependent decisions in order, with the actor offering a recommended answer alongside each question.

source.quote: Interview me relentlessly about every aspect of this until we reach a shared understanding. Walk down each branch of the decision tree, resolving dependencies between decisions one-by-one. For each question, provide your recommended answer.

trigger: grilling workflow is active
outcome: every branch of the decision tree is walked and resolved with a recorded recommendation
notes: Requires judgment (identify the decision tree, order dependencies, form a recommendation) — an actor-stage checkpoint, not deterministic machinery.
rationale: Judgment is required (branch identification, dependency ordering, recommendation authoring) — fits 6.4's actor-stage test; the loop itself is a meaningful checkpoint (would survive a reimplementation of the interview mechanism).
alternatives_considered: helper (rejected: it requires interpretive judgment about dependency order and a recommendation, not repeatable deterministic machinery)

statement: Within the interview loop, only one question is posed at a time, and the actor waits for the user's answer before asking the next.

source.quote: Ask the questions one at a time, waiting for feedback on each question before continuing. Asking multiple questions at once is bewildering.

trigger: the interview loop is asking a question
outcome: one confirmed answer exists before the next question is posed
rationale: A rule governing how the interview-loop stage is crossed (pacing/turn-taking), not itself an independent checkpoint or reusable procedure.
alternatives_considered: separate stage 'ask-one-question' (rejected: it is a constraint on the single interview-loop checkpoint, not a distinct durable milestone)

statement: The interview loop draws a firm line: facts discoverable by exploring the environment must be looked up by the actor; only genuine decisions are put to the user, and the actor waits for the user's answer on each.

source.quote: If a *fact* can be found by exploring the environment (filesystem, tools, etc.), look it up rather than asking me. The *decisions*, though, are mine — put each one to me and wait for my answer.

trigger: a question arises during the interview loop
outcome: facts are resolved autonomously; decisions are resolved only by explicit user answer
notes: An authority-boundary rule local to the grilling workflow, distinct from (but echoing the shape of) sergeant-rs's own actor/user authority separation.
rationale: Governs how each question in the interview-loop checkpoint is classified and answered; not itself a separate checkpoint.
alternatives_considered: workflow-level invariant (rejected: scoped specifically to what happens inside the interview-loop checkpoint, not a repository-wide rule)

statement: The workflow may not proceed to action until the user explicitly confirms shared understanding has been reached.

source.quote: Do not act on it until I confirm we have reached a shared understanding.

trigger: the interview loop has walked all decision-tree branches
outcome: an explicit user confirmation of shared understanding exists before any action is taken
notes: This is the workflow's completion checkpoint — distinguishable from the interview-loop stage itself.
rationale: A durable, operator-relevant boundary: would this checkpoint survive a reimplementation of the interview mechanism? Yes — 'do not act without explicit confirmation' is a meaningful gate regardless of how questions are asked.
alternatives_considered: stage-context of interview-loop (rejected: it is a distinct terminal gate the whole workflow depends on, not a rule about crossing the question-asking checkpoint)

statement: prototype is a workflow that builds throwaway code to answer a specific design question, either about logic/state or about UI appearance.

source.quote: description: Build a throwaway prototype to answer a design question. Use when the user wants to sanity-check whether a state model or logic feels right, or explore what a UI should look like.

trigger: user wants to sanity-check a state model/logic or explore UI appearance
outcome: the design question is answered and the answer is captured; the prototype code itself is discarded from main
rationale: Recognizable trigger, bounded outcome (an answered design question), completion condition (capture step) — reusable procedural outcome per 6.2. Proposal 8.2 independently names this a stress case for conditional procedure.
alternatives_considered: two independent workflows, 'logic-prototype' and 'ui-prototype' (rejected: they share one trigger surface, one set of rules, and one capture procedure — the branch is a stage inside one workflow, not two workflows)

statement: The defining premise of the workflow: a prototype exists only to answer one question, and the nature of that question determines which branch and shape the prototype takes.

source.quote: A prototype is **throwaway code that answers a question**. The question decides the shape.

trigger: n/a — foundational premise
outcome: all subsequent branch/shape decisions trace back to the question
rationale: This is the workflow's identity statement, not a checkpoint — it frames why the workflow branches at all.
alternatives_considered: stage-context of select-branch (rejected: this is the whole workflow's identity statement framing why both branches exist, not a rule governing how the select-branch checkpoint itself is crossed)
agents-invariant (rejected: scoped specifically to the prototype workflow, not a repository-wide rule)

statement: The first checkpoint of the prototype workflow is determining which of the two question-types (logic/state vs. UI) is being asked, using the prompt, surrounding code, or the user directly.

source.quote: Identify which question is being answered — from the user's prompt, the surrounding code, or by asking if the user is around:

trigger: prototype workflow invoked
outcome: one of the two branches (logic or UI) is selected
rationale: Requires judgment among alternatives (6.4) and getting it wrong 'wastes the whole prototype' per the workflow's own text — a meaningful, judgment-bearing checkpoint.
alternatives_considered: helper (rejected: branch selection requires interpreting ambiguous natural-language/code signals, not a deterministic lookup)

statement: When the question is about appearance, the workflow routes to the UI-prototype branch, which produces several structurally different UI variants switchable in-browser.

source.quote: - **"What should this look like?"** → [UI.md](UI.md). Generate several radically different UI variations on a single route, switchable via a URL search param and a floating bottom bar.

trigger: the question is about what something should look like
outcome: the UI-prototype branch is selected and its variant/switcher shape is set as the target artifact
rationale: Part of the routing table for the select-branch checkpoint; defines one of the two destinations rather than being its own checkpoint.

statement: When the branch choice is ambiguous and the user cannot be reached, the workflow falls back to a heuristic based on the surrounding code's shape and records the assumption explicitly in the prototype, rather than blocking.

source.quote: The two branches produce very different artifacts — getting this wrong wastes the whole prototype. If the question is genuinely ambiguous and the user isn't reachable, default to whichever branch better matches the surrounding code (a backend module → logic; a page or component → UI) and state the assumption at the top of the prototype.

trigger: the branch question is ambiguous and the user is unreachable
outcome: a branch is chosen by heuristic and the assumption is recorded, rather than the workflow stalling
notes: Contrasts with sergeant-rs's own 'ambiguity fails closed' invariant (CLAUDE.md 4.3): here ambiguity resolves via a stated, reversible assumption rather than blocking — worth flagging for classification review as a case where a source workflow's ambiguity-handling differs from the target runtime's default posture.
rationale: A fallback rule for crossing the select-branch checkpoint under ambiguity; not a new checkpoint itself.
alternatives_considered: fail-closed on ambiguity (considered — this is the opposite policy the source workflow actually specifies; recorded, not silently normalized to sergeant-rs's default)

statement: Prototype code must be placed near its eventual real-code home and clearly named as throwaway, and any throwaway route must follow the host project's existing routing convention rather than inventing a new structure.

source.quote: 1. **Throwaway from day one, and clearly marked as such.** Locate the prototype code close to where it will actually be used (next to the module or page it's prototyping for) so context is obvious — but name it so a casual reader can see it's a prototype, not production. For throwaway UI routes, obey whatever routing convention the project already uses; don't invent a new top-level structure.

trigger: a prototype is being created (either branch)
outcome: the prototype is discoverable, clearly marked, and does not add a new structural convention to the project
rationale: A rule reused by both the logic and UI branches (6.6): keep it local to the prototype workflow rather than duplicating it inside each branch's own doc.
alternatives_considered: stage-context duplicated in each branch (rejected: the throwaway-marking/routing-convention rule is identical in intent for both the logic and UI branches; one shared-context entry avoids two near-duplicate copies drifting apart)

statement: A prototype must be runnable with a single command through the host project's existing task runner.

source.quote: 2. **One command to run.** Whatever the project's existing task runner supports — `pnpm <name>`, `python <path>`, `bun <path>`, etc. The user must be able to start it without thinking.

trigger: a prototype is being created
outcome: the user can start the prototype with one command
rationale: Reused verbatim-in-spirit by both LOGIC.md (step 5) and UI.md; kept local to the prototype workflow.
alternatives_considered: stage-context duplicated in each branch (rejected: the one-command-to-run rule is reused verbatim-in-spirit by both LOGIC.md step 5 and UI.md; a single shared-context entry is the non-duplicating representation)

statement: Prototype state defaults to in-memory only; persistence is added only when the question is specifically about persistence, and then only via an obviously-disposable scratch store.

source.quote: 3. **No persistence by default.** State lives in memory. Persistence is the thing the prototype is _checking_, not something it should depend on. If the question explicitly involves a database, hit a scratch DB or a local file with a clear "PROTOTYPE — wipe me" name.

trigger: a prototype is being created
outcome: the prototype does not depend on durable storage unless persistence is itself the question
rationale: A workflow-local rule reused by both branches.
alternatives_considered: stage-context local to one branch (rejected: both the logic and UI branches independently need the no-persistence-by-default rule; a shared-context entry avoids restating it twice)

statement: Every user-visible action in a prototype must re-surface the full relevant state so the user can observe what changed.

source.quote: 5. **Surface the state.** After every action (logic) or on every variant switch (UI), print or render the full relevant state so the user can see what changed.

trigger: a user action or variant switch occurs in the prototype
outcome: the current state is visibly rendered
rationale: Reused by both LOGIC.md's re-render rule and UI.md's switcher; the underlying principle is stated once at the workflow level.
alternatives_considered: stage-context duplicated per branch (rejected: LOGIC.md's re-render rule and UI.md's switcher behaviour both restate this principle; kept as one shared-context entry at the workflow level instead)

statement: Once a prototype has answered its question, the validated decision is folded into real code while the prototype itself is preserved as a primary source on a throwaway branch (not main), with the answer and question recorded on the implementation issue or a commit, and only the validated decision surviving on the main branch.

source.quote: 6. **Capture it when done.** Fold any validated decision into the real code, then capture the prototype itself as a **primary source**: commit it to a throwaway branch, out of main, and leave a context pointer to that branch on the implementation issue. Capture the answer too — the verdict and the question it settled — in the issue or a commit. The main branch keeps only the validated decision.

trigger: the prototype has answered its question
outcome: real code reflects the validated decision; the prototype and its verdict are durably recorded outside main
rationale: A durable, operator-relevant checkpoint distinct from building the prototype: would survive a reimplementation of the throwaway-code mechanism, and its absence would lose the prototype's evidentiary value entirely.
alternatives_considered: shared-context (rejected: this is not merely a rule crossed inside another checkpoint — it is itself the workflow's terminal, evidence-bearing checkpoint)

statement: The logic-prototype branch builds a small interactive terminal app so the user can hand-drive a state model through the cases that are hard to evaluate on paper.

source.quote: A tiny interactive terminal app that lets the user drive a state model by hand. Use this when the question is about **business logic, state transitions, or data shape** — the kind of thing that looks reasonable on paper but only feels wrong once you push it through real cases.

trigger: the branch question is about business logic, state transitions, or data shape
outcome: an interactive terminal app exists that lets the user push the state model through concrete cases
rationale: Defines the identity/purpose of the logic sub-branch, echoing the routing already established at the parent workflow's select-branch checkpoint.
alternatives_considered: stage-context of select-branch (rejected: this defines the logic sub-branch's own identity/purpose as a distinct downstream procedure, not a rule for crossing the parent's branch-selection checkpoint)
separate standalone workflow 'logic-prototype' (rejected: it has no independent trigger — it is only entered via the parent prototype workflow's branch-selection checkpoint)

statement: Before any code is written, the actor records the state model and the exact question the prototype answers, so the question can be checked against the eventual result even if the user returns to it later.

source.quote: Before writing code, write down what state model and what question you're prototyping. One paragraph, in the prototype's README or a comment at the top of the file. A logic prototype that answers the wrong question is pure waste — make the question explicit so it can be checked later, whether the user is watching now or returning to it AFK.

trigger: the logic-prototype branch has been selected
outcome: a written statement of the question and state model exists before code is written
rationale: A durable checkpoint: an unstated question is called out as 'pure waste' in the source text itself — the source explicitly treats this as a milestone worth protecting.
alternatives_considered: helper (rejected: the source explicitly frames an unstated question as 'pure waste' — a durability/judgment checkpoint whose absence loses the prototype's evidentiary value, not deterministic subordinate machinery)
stage-context of logic-build-module (rejected: it is a distinct, prior checkpoint — the question and state model are written down before any module is built)

statement: The logic under test must be isolated behind a small, pure interface that can later be lifted into the real codebase; only the terminal UI shell around it is truly throwaway.

source.quote: Put the actual logic — the bit that's answering the question — behind a small, pure interface that could be lifted out and dropped into the real codebase later. The TUI around it is throwaway; the logic module shouldn't be.

trigger: building the logic-prototype
outcome: the validated logic module is reusable independent of the throwaway TUI
rationale: A durable design checkpoint distinguishing what survives (the logic module) from what doesn't (the TUI) — central to the branch's later capture stage.
alternatives_considered: stage-context of logic-build-tui (rejected: isolating the pure module is a separate, prior design checkpoint from building the TUI shell around it)
helper (rejected: choosing the pure-interface boundary is a design judgment central to what survives capture, not deterministic machinery)

statement: The logic module must stay pure — no I/O, no terminal code, no console output used for control flow — and the dependency direction is one-way: the TUI imports the logic module, never the reverse.

source.quote: Pick whichever shape best fits the question being asked, *not* whichever is easiest to wire to a TUI. Keep it pure: no I/O, no terminal code, no `console.log` for control flow. The TUI imports it and calls into it; nothing flows the other direction.

trigger: implementing the isolated logic module
outcome: the logic module has no dependency on the TUI shell
rationale: A purity/dependency-direction constraint governing how the logic-build-module checkpoint is crossed correctly.

statement: The terminal UI re-renders the full frame from scratch on every update rather than appending output, so the user always sees one stable current view.

source.quote: Build it as a **lightweight TUI** — on every tick, clear the screen (`console.clear()` / `print("\033[2J\033[H")` / equivalent) and re-render the whole frame. The user should always see one stable view, not an ever-growing scrollback.

trigger: building the interactive terminal shell
outcome: the terminal shows one current frame, never an accumulating scrollback
rationale: A rendering-pattern rule for the build-TUI checkpoint; the concrete escape codes are illustrative, the clear-and-redraw principle is the durable part.

statement: After each user action, the shell replaces the displayed frame entirely rather than appending to it.

source.quote: 3. **Re-render** the full frame after every action — don't append, replace.

trigger: a user action has just been dispatched
outcome: the displayed frame reflects only the current state, not a history of prior frames
rationale: Restates and pins the replace-not-append rendering discipline as an explicit loop step.

statement: The logic prototype is wired into the host project's existing task runner so it can be started by name rather than by remembering a file path.

source.quote: Add a script to the project's existing task runner (`package.json` scripts, `Makefile`, `justfile`, `pyproject.toml`). The user should run `pnpm run <prototype-name>` or equivalent — never need to remember a path.

trigger: the logic prototype is ready to hand to the user
outcome: the prototype is runnable via the project's normal task-runner invocation
rationale: Refines the workflow-level 'one command to run' shared-context rule with the logic branch's concrete mechanism (task-runner entry).

statement: For the logic branch specifically, the capture stage means the validated reducer/state-machine/function set is absorbed into the real module while the TUI shell is preserved only on the throwaway branch.

source.quote: Once the prototype has answered its question, capture the answer, then capture the prototype the way the [SKILL](SKILL.md) describes. The logic-specific mapping: the validated reducer / machine / function set lifts into the real module (the decision, absorbed); the TUI shell rides along to the throwaway branch that keeps the prototype as a primary source.

trigger: the logic-prototype question has been answered
outcome: the real codebase gains the validated logic module; the TUI shell is archived, not merged
rationale: Branch-specific detail refining the shared 'capture' stage already established at the parent workflow level (BU for prototype/SKILL.md item 6).

statement: The throwaway TUI shell must never reach production; only the underlying logic module is meant to survive.

source.quote: - **Don't ship the TUI shell into production.** The shell is optimised for being driven by hand from a terminal. The logic module behind it is the bit worth keeping.

trigger: capturing or reviewing prototype output
outcome: production code never contains the prototype's TUI shell
notes: Parallels UI.md's 'hidden in production builds' guard and its own promote-to-production anti-pattern — a repeated pattern across both branches worth flagging in shared-context-map.md.
rationale: A boundary condition on what may cross into the capture stage's output.

statement: The UI-prototype branch produces several structurally distinct UI variants on one route, switchable live in the browser, from which the user picks or recombines before the rest is discarded.

source.quote: Generate **several radically different UI variations** on a single route, switchable from a floating bottom bar. The user flips between variants in the browser, picks one (or steals bits from each), then throws the rest away.

trigger: the branch question is about what something should look like
outcome: several in-browser-switchable UI variants exist for the user to compare
rationale: Defines the identity/purpose of the UI sub-branch, mirroring the LOGIC.md header BU's role for the logic branch.
alternatives_considered: stage-context of select-branch (rejected: this defines the UI sub-branch's own identity/purpose, not a crossing-rule for the parent's branch-selection checkpoint)
separate standalone workflow 'ui-prototype' (rejected: no independent trigger; reached only via the parent workflow's branch selection)

statement: The UI branch prefers mounting variants inside an existing page (sub-shape A) over a standalone throwaway route (sub-shape B), because judging a variant against the app's real surrounding context is more informative than judging it in isolation.

source.quote: A UI prototype is much easier to judge when it's **butting up against the rest of the app** — real header, real sidebar, real data, real density. A throwaway route on its own is a vacuum: every variant looks fine in isolation. Default to sub-shape A whenever there's a plausible existing page to host the variants. Only reach for sub-shape B if the prototype genuinely has no nearby home.

trigger: the UI-prototype branch has been selected
outcome: sub-shape A is chosen unless no existing page can host the variants
rationale: A judgment-bearing checkpoint (choosing among two structurally different hosting strategies) with a stated default and an explicit escape hatch — a meaningful boundary distinct from picking the logic/UI branch itself.
alternatives_considered: stage-context of select-branch (rejected: this is a second, UI-branch-local decision point, not a detail of the parent workflow's branch-selection checkpoint)

statement: When sub-shape B is used, the new throwaway route must follow the project's existing routing convention and be named so it is obviously a prototype.

source.quote: Create a **throwaway route** following whatever routing convention the project already uses — don't invent a new top-level structure. Name it so it's obviously a prototype (e.g. include the word `prototype` in the path or filename). Same `?variant=` pattern.

trigger: sub-shape B has been chosen
outcome: the throwaway route is discoverable as a prototype and does not introduce a new routing convention
rationale: A rule for correctly crossing the ui-select-subshape checkpoint when sub-shape B is the outcome; echoes the parent workflow's shared 'don't invent a new top-level structure' rule (prototype/SKILL.md item 1).

statement: The UI branch defaults to producing three variants and caps at five, beyond which additional variants are considered noise rather than useful signal.

source.quote: Default to **3 variants**. More than 5 stops being radically different and starts being noise — cap there.

trigger: generating UI variants
outcome: the number of variants produced falls between the default of three and a hard cap of five
rationale: A concrete numeric bound governing the generate-variants checkpoint.

statement: Each UI variant must differ structurally (layout, information hierarchy, primary affordance), not merely cosmetically; if two drafts converge, one must be redone with an explicit constraint forcing structural divergence.

source.quote: Variants must be **structurally different** — different layout, different information hierarchy, different primary affordance, not just different colours. Three slightly-tweaked card grids isn't a UI prototype, it's wallpaper. If two drafts come out too similar, redo one with explicit "do not use a card grid" guidance.

trigger: drafting UI variants
outcome: every variant produced is structurally distinct from the others
rationale: A quality bar for what counts as a valid crossing of the generate-variants checkpoint.

statement: The variant switcher UI must be gated off in production builds so that an accidental merge of prototype code cannot expose it to real users.

source.quote: - Hidden in production builds — gate on `process.env.NODE_ENV !== 'production'` or an equivalent check, so a stray prototype merge can't ship the bar to users.

trigger: building the variant switcher
outcome: the switcher never renders in a production build
notes: Parallels LOGIC.md's 'don't ship the TUI shell into production' anti-pattern — a repeated cross-branch safety rule worth noting in shared-context-map.md.
rationale: A safety constraint on the build-switcher checkpoint.

statement: After building the variants, the actor hands the user the URL and variant keys; the most useful feedback typically recombines pieces across variants rather than picking one outright.

source.quote: Surface the URL (and the `?variant=` keys). The user will flip through whenever they get to it. The interesting feedback is usually **"I want the header from B with the sidebar from C"** — that's the actual design they want.

trigger: the variant switcher is built and ready
outcome: the user has a shareable URL to explore variants and can express cross-variant preferences
rationale: A durable hand-off checkpoint distinct from building the variants — marks the transition from actor-driven generation to user-driven evaluation.
alternatives_considered: stage-context of ui-generate-variants (rejected: hand-off is a distinct transition from actor-driven generation to user-driven evaluation, not a rule about how variants are generated)
helper (rejected: it marks a durable, operator-relevant transition point, not deterministic subordinate machinery)

statement: For sub-shape A, capture means folding the winning variant into the existing page and removing the other variants and the switcher from the main branch.

source.quote: - **Sub-shape A** — fold the winner into the existing page; drop the losing variants and the switcher from main.

trigger: the user has picked a winning variant (sub-shape A)
outcome: main contains only the winning variant, folded into the existing page
rationale: Sub-shape-A-specific detail refining the shared capture stage from prototype/SKILL.md.

statement: For sub-shape B, capture means promoting the winning variant to a real, permanent route and removing the throwaway route and switcher from main.

source.quote: - **Sub-shape B** — promote the winning variant to a real route; drop the throwaway route and the switcher from main.

trigger: the user has picked a winning variant (sub-shape B)
outcome: main contains a real route for the winning variant; the throwaway route and switcher are gone
rationale: Sub-shape-B-specific detail refining the same shared capture stage.

statement: UI variants must not perform real mutations; any mutation a variant needs should hit a stub, keeping the prototype scoped to appearance rather than backend correctness.

source.quote: - **Wiring variants to real mutations.** Read-only prototypes are fine. If a variant needs to mutate, point it at a stub — the question is "what should this look like", not "does the backend work".

trigger: building or wiring a UI variant
outcome: no UI variant performs a real write against production systems
rationale: A scope-boundary constraint on what a variant may do while crossing the generate/wire checkpoints.

statement: Winning variant code must be rewritten to production standards when folded in, not merged as-is, since it was written under prototype constraints such as no tests and minimal error handling.

source.quote: - **Promoting the prototype directly to production.** The variant code was written under prototype constraints (no tests, minimal error handling). Rewrite it properly when you fold it in.

trigger: folding the winning variant into real code (capture)
outcome: the code that lands in production has been rewritten to meet normal production standards
rationale: A quality gate on the capture stage's output, paired with the LOGIC.md capture-time production-safety rule.

statement: research is a workflow that investigates a question against high-trust primary sources and writes the findings to a Markdown file in the repository.

source.quote: description: Investigate a question against high-trust primary sources and capture the findings as a Markdown file in the repo. Use when the user wants a topic researched, docs or API facts gathered, or reading legwork delegated to a background agent.

trigger: user wants a topic researched or reading legwork delegated
outcome: a Markdown file exists in the repo capturing source-cited findings
rationale: Recognizable trigger, bounded outcome (a findings file), completion condition — reusable procedural outcome per 6.2.
alternatives_considered: stage of some larger workflow (rejected: research has its own independent trigger — a delegated question — and is not entered as part of another procedure)
agents-invariant (rejected: this is a bounded procedure with its own trigger, outcome, and completion condition, not a standing repository-wide rule)

statement: The research workflow is delegated to a background/asynchronous execution context so the requester's foreground work is not blocked while sources are read.

source.quote: Spin up a **background agent** to do the research, so you keep working while it reads.

trigger: a research question is delegated
outcome: the requester continues other work while research proceeds independently
notes: This asks for asynchronous, non-blocking delegation of one procedure while other work continues. Sergeant-rs's own daemon/Work model already provides durable, independent execution of a dispatched unit of work with later notification (the whole point of the journal-backed daemon) — so this does not name a fact the runtime doesn't already own; it is evidence for how an actor-stage workflow should be invoked (as a dispatched Work), not evidence of a missing capability.
rationale: An execution-mode note attached to the workflow's trigger/invocation, not a separate checkpoint.
alternatives_considered: engine-gap: asynchronous multi-Work delegation while a parent context continues (considered and rejected — sergeant-rs's Work dispatch + later notification model already satisfies 'start it, keep working, get told when it's done'; no new durable fact is named that the runtime doesn't already own)

statement: Research must be conducted against primary sources (official docs, source code, specs, first-party APIs) rather than secondary summaries, with every claim traced back to its owning source.

source.quote: 1. Investigate the question against **primary sources** — official docs, source code, specs, first-party APIs — not a secondary write-up of them. Follow every claim back to the source that owns it.

trigger: the research workflow is investigating
outcome: every claim in the findings traces to a primary source
rationale: A durable evidentiary standard for the investigate checkpoint — the source explicitly distinguishes primary from secondary sourcing as a quality bar operators would care about.
alternatives_considered: stage-context of write-findings (rejected: this is an evidentiary standard governing the investigation itself, prior to and independent of writing the findings file)
shared-context (rejected: local to a single-stage-pair workflow with no second stage to share the rule with)

statement: The investigation's output is a single Markdown file where every claim carries a source citation.

source.quote: 2. Write the findings to a single Markdown file, citing each claim's source.

trigger: investigation is complete
outcome: a single cited Markdown findings file exists
rationale: The artifact-producing checkpoint of the workflow — the durable outcome the trigger promised.
alternatives_considered: stage-context of investigate (rejected: this is the workflow's artifact-producing checkpoint — the durable outcome the trigger promised — not a rule about how investigation is conducted)
helper (rejected: producing the cited findings file is the checkpoint operators care about crossing, not a deterministic subordinate step)

statement: The findings file is placed according to the repository's existing note-keeping convention, or in a sensible location (with the choice explicitly stated) if no convention exists.

source.quote: 3. Save it where the repo already keeps such notes; match the existing convention, and if there is none, put it somewhere sensible and say where.

trigger: the findings file is being saved
outcome: the file lands in a discoverable, convention-consistent (or explicitly justified) location
rationale: A placement rule governing how the write-findings checkpoint is correctly crossed.

statement: resolving-merge-conflicts is a workflow that resolves an in-progress git merge or rebase conflict to completion.

source.quote: description: "Use when you need to resolve an in-progress git merge/rebase conflict."

trigger: a merge or rebase is in progress with conflicts
outcome: the merge/rebase is completed with all conflicts resolved and checks passing
rationale: Clear trigger (in-progress conflict), bounded outcome (finished merge/rebase), sequential checkpoints below — the proposal's diagnosing-bugs-style 'strong low-ambiguity reference workflow' pattern.
alternatives_considered: stage of some larger workflow (rejected: it has its own independent trigger — an in-progress merge/rebase conflict — not entered as a step of another procedure)
helper (rejected: it is a multi-checkpoint, judgment-bearing procedure with its own sequential stages, not a deterministic subordinate step)

statement: The first checkpoint establishes the current merge/rebase state by inspecting git history and the conflicting files.

source.quote: 1. **See the current state** of the merge/rebase. Check git history, and the conflicting files.

trigger: the workflow begins
outcome: the actor has an accurate picture of what is conflicting and why
rationale: A meaningful starting checkpoint: skipping it risks resolving conflicts blind — would survive a reimplementation of however 'state' is inspected.
alternatives_considered: helper (rejected: accurately establishing what is conflicting and why is a judgment-bearing checkpoint whose absence risks resolving conflicts blind, not deterministic machinery)
stage-context of research-intent (rejected: assessing state is a distinct, prior checkpoint from tracing per-conflict intent)

statement: For each conflict, the actor traces the original intent behind each side's change via commit messages, PRs, and issues/tickets before attempting resolution.

source.quote: 2. **Find the primary sources** for each conflict. Understand deeply why each change was made, and what the original intent was. Read the commit messages, check the PRs, check original issues/tickets.

trigger: conflicting hunks have been identified
outcome: the intent behind each conflicting change is understood before it is resolved
rationale: A judgment-heavy checkpoint (6.4): deep understanding of intent from primary sources, not deterministic machinery.
alternatives_considered: stage-context of resolve-hunks (rejected: tracing intent is a separate, judgment-heavy checkpoint that must complete before resolution, not a rule for crossing resolve-hunks itself)
helper (rejected: deep primary-source investigation of intent is interpretive judgment, not a deterministic lookup)

statement: Each conflicting hunk is resolved by preserving both sides' intent where possible, or by picking the side matching the merge's stated goal and recording the trade-off when incompatible; resolution must never invent new behavior, and the merge/rebase must always be carried to completion rather than aborted.

source.quote: 3. **Resolve each hunk.** Preserve both intents where possible. Where incompatible, pick the one matching the merge's stated goal and note the trade-off. Do **not** invent new behaviour. Always resolve; never `--abort`.

trigger: conflict intents are understood
outcome: every hunk is resolved consistent with recorded intent, with no invented behavior, and the operation is never abandoned via --abort
notes: The 'always resolve; never abort' clause is a strict boundary condition distinct from the resolution judgment itself, worth flagging in classification review as a candidate for its own stage-context rule.
rationale: The core judgment checkpoint of the workflow, with an explicit hard constraint (never abort) attached.
alternatives_considered: stage-context of research-intent (rejected: this is the workflow's core judgment checkpoint — actually resolving hunks under a hard constraint — not a rule governing the prior intent-research checkpoint)
helper (rejected: resolving each hunk under a 'never abort' constraint is the durable checkpoint operators care about, not deterministic subordinate machinery)

statement: After resolving conflicts, the actor discovers and runs the project's automated checks in the order typecheck, then tests, then format, fixing anything the merge broke.

source.quote: 4. Discover the project's **automated checks** and run them — typically typecheck, then tests, then format. Fix anything the merge broke.

trigger: all hunks are resolved
outcome: the project's own automated checks pass and any merge-induced breakage is fixed
notes: The ordering (typecheck, then tests, then format) is a concrete deterministic sequencing detail that may recur elsewhere in the corpus (e.g. no-mistakes' validation ordering, P2) — worth a cross-reference in helper-map.md if confirmed there.
rationale: A durable checkpoint (operators would care whether validation ran and passed) with a specific ordered helper sequence subordinate to it.
alternatives_considered: helper only (rejected: 'run checks and fix breakage' is itself a checkpoint operators care about crossing, not merely a deterministic sub-step of another checkpoint)

statement: The workflow concludes by staging and committing everything, and, if rebasing, continuing until every commit has been rebased.

source.quote: 5. **Finish the merge/rebase.** Stage everything and commit. If rebasing, continue the rebase process until all commits are rebased.

trigger: validation has passed
outcome: the merge or rebase is fully completed and committed
rationale: The terminal completion checkpoint of the workflow.
alternatives_considered: stage-context of resolve-hunks or validate (rejected: finishing and committing is a separate terminal checkpoint, not a rule for crossing an earlier stage)
helper (rejected: this is the workflow's durable completion checkpoint, not a deterministic subordinate step of another stage)

statement: triage is a workflow that moves issues and qualifying external PRs through a fixed state machine of category and state roles, ending in an agent-ready brief or another terminal disposition.

source.quote: description: Move issues and external PRs through a state machine of triage roles — categorise, verify, grill if needed, and write agent-ready briefs.

trigger: the maintainer wants to evaluate or advance an issue or PR
outcome: the item carries an up-to-date category and state role, with any required brief/comment posted
rationale: Recognizable trigger (/triage or item-specific request), bounded per-invocation outcome (role applied, comment/brief posted), and an explicit state-machine structure — a reusable procedural outcome per 6.2.
alternatives_considered: stage of some larger workflow (rejected: triage is independently triggered by a maintainer request or /triage invocation, not entered as a step of another procedure)
shared-helper (rejected: this is the top-level bounded procedure itself, not a reusable subordinate step invoked by other workflows)

statement: The triage workflow treats a qualifying external PR as an issue with attached code, reusing the same roles and state machine with a small number of documented deltas.

source.quote: If this repo treats external pull requests as a request surface (see the issue-tracker config), triage covers them too: **a PR is an issue with attached code** — same roles, same states, same machine, with a few deltas marked "for a PR" below. Resolve a bare `#42` to an issue or PR per the tracker config.

trigger: the tracker config treats external PRs as a request surface
outcome: a PR is triaged through the identical role/state vocabulary as an issue
rationale: Defines the scope of what the triage workflow's single state machine covers, rather than being its own checkpoint.
alternatives_considered: stage-context of a specific checkpoint (rejected: this is a workflow-wide scoping rule defining what the whole state machine covers, not a rule for crossing one particular checkpoint)
shared-context (rejected: it defines the workflow's own subject matter/boundary, not a rule reused across multiple stages within one crossing)

statement: Every tracker-visible artifact (comment or issue) the triage workflow posts must be prefixed with an AI-authorship disclaimer.

source.quote: Every comment or issue posted to the issue tracker during triage **must** start with this disclaimer:

trigger: the workflow is about to post any comment or issue
outcome: every posted artifact discloses it was AI-generated during triage
rationale: A rule crossed at every posting action throughout the workflow (multiple stages), not tied to one checkpoint — kept as a workflow-local shared rule per 6.6.
alternatives_considered: stage-context of apply-outcome (rejected: the disclaimer applies to every posting action across multiple stages — gather-context comments, recommend, apply-outcome — not just one checkpoint)

statement: needs-triage is a state in the triage state machine meaning the maintainer still needs to evaluate the item.

source.quote: - `needs-triage` — maintainer needs to evaluate

trigger: an item is unlabeled or returns from needs-info
outcome: the item is queued for maintainer evaluation
rationale: A named, durable, operator-relevant state in the triage state machine — exactly the kind of checkpoint 6.3 asks about (would this state still exist under any implementation of triage? yes).
alternatives_considered: stage-context of a different state (rejected: needs-triage is itself a named, durable state that would survive any reimplementation of triage, not a rule for crossing a different state's checkpoint)
shared-context (rejected: it is a state a specific item occupies, not a rule reused across the workflow's own checkpoint crossings)

statement: needs-info is a state meaning the item is waiting on the reporter to supply more information before triage can proceed.

source.quote: - `needs-info` — waiting on reporter for more information

trigger: the actor cannot proceed without more information from the reporter
outcome: the item is parked pending reporter reply
notes: Directly evidences the proposal's planned needs_input/waiting execute-stage semantics (9.5 example, 15.4) — a real-world precedent for that feature, not itself a new engine requirement.
rationale: A durable waiting checkpoint whose resumption is handled elsewhere in this file (see the 'Resuming a previous session' BU).
alternatives_considered: stage-context of needs-triage or apply-outcome (rejected: needs-info is its own durable, resumable state, distinct from the entry state and from the act of applying an outcome)
helper (rejected: it names a state operators must be able to observe and resume, not deterministic subordinate machinery)

statement: ready-for-agent is a state meaning the item is fully specified and ready for an autonomous agent to act on.

source.quote: - `ready-for-agent` — fully specified, ready for an AFK agent

trigger: verification and (if needed) grilling are complete
outcome: an agent-ready brief exists and the item is queued for agent pickup
rationale: A terminal-for-triage, durable state whose entry action (posting a brief) is itself a checkpoint operators care about.
alternatives_considered: stage-context of apply-outcome (rejected: ready-for-agent is itself a terminal, durable state whose entry action — posting a brief — is a checkpoint, not merely a rule for crossing apply-outcome)
helper (rejected: it names a durable state operators track, not deterministic subordinate machinery)

statement: ready-for-human is a state meaning the item needs a human to implement it rather than an agent.

source.quote: - `ready-for-human` — needs human implementation

trigger: the item cannot be delegated to an agent
outcome: the item is queued for human implementation with reasoning recorded
rationale: A terminal-for-triage state parallel to ready-for-agent but for non-delegable work.
alternatives_considered: stage-context of ready-for-agent (rejected: it is a parallel but distinct terminal state, not a rule about the agent-ready state)
helper (rejected: it names a durable state, not deterministic subordinate machinery)

statement: wontfix is a state meaning the item will not be actioned, closed either because it is already implemented, a rejected bug, or a rejected enhancement.

source.quote: - `wontfix` — will not be actioned

trigger: the item is determined not to warrant action
outcome: the item is closed with a disposition-specific comment
rationale: A terminal state with three distinct closing sub-branches captured as separate stage-context BUs below.
alternatives_considered: stage-context of apply-outcome (rejected: wontfix is itself a terminal state with three distinct closing sub-branches captured separately, not merely a crossing rule)
helper (rejected: it names a durable terminal state, not deterministic subordinate machinery)

statement: The state machine enforces exactly one category role and one state role per item at any time; a conflicting state role must be flagged to the maintainer before any further action.

source.quote: Every triaged issue should carry exactly one category role and one state role. If state roles conflict, flag it and ask the maintainer before doing anything else.

trigger: an item's roles are being read or set
outcome: no item ever carries conflicting state roles without maintainer resolution first
notes: An ambiguity-fails-closed-style constraint local to the triage state machine, echoing (without being identical to) sergeant-rs's own ambiguity invariant.
rationale: A data-integrity constraint on the state machine as a whole, not one checkpoint's crossing rule.
alternatives_considered: stage-context of a single checkpoint (rejected: the one-role-per-item invariant applies whenever any state role is read or set anywhere in the workflow, not one specific checkpoint)

statement: The triage state machine's transition graph starts at needs-triage, fans out to needs-info/ready-for-agent/ready-for-human/wontfix, loops needs-info back to needs-triage on reporter reply, and allows the maintainer to override any transition at will, with unusual transitions flagged for confirmation first.

source.quote: State transitions: an unlabeled issue normally goes to `needs-triage` first; from there it moves to `needs-info`, `ready-for-agent`, `ready-for-human`, or `wontfix`. `needs-info` returns to `needs-triage` once the reporter replies. The maintainer can override at any time — flag transitions that look unusual and ask before proceeding.

trigger: an item's state needs to change
outcome: the item's next state matches the defined transition graph unless the maintainer explicitly overrides it
notes: This is a non-linear state machine (loops, maintainer override at any time), unlike the corpus's more linear reference workflows (diagnosing-bugs, resolving-merge-conflicts). Considered as an engine-gap candidate: does sergeant-rs need new durable-fact ownership to represent this? No — the state lives in the external issue tracker (labels), not in sergeant's own journal; each triage invocation is a bounded actor-stage procedure reading/writing that external state, and repeated invocation over time already covers the loop/override behavior without the runtime owning new ordering, identity, retry, or authorization semantics.
rationale: Defines the shape of the state machine the workflow's per-invocation stages operate against.
alternatives_considered: engine-gap: sergeant owning a persistent, loop-capable issue-state machine (considered and rejected — the issue tracker already owns and persists this state; sergeant's role is one bounded procedure invocation per triage action, which the current actor-stage model already supports)

statement: The workflow's trigger is a natural-language maintainer request, interpreted by the actor to select which triage action to take.

source.quote: The maintainer invokes `/triage` and describes what they want in natural language. Interpret the request and act. Examples:

trigger: the maintainer invokes triage
outcome: the actor selects and executes the matching triage action
rationale: Defines the trigger/invocation shape for the whole workflow.
alternatives_considered: stage-context of a specific checkpoint (rejected: this defines the entire workflow's invocation/trigger shape, not a rule inside one checkpoint)
agents-invariant (rejected: scoped specifically to triage's own invocation pattern, not a repository-wide rule)

statement: When asked what needs attention, the workflow queries the tracker and presents three fixed buckets ordered oldest-first.

source.quote: Query the issue tracker and present three buckets, oldest first:

trigger: the maintainer asks what needs attention
outcome: three ordered buckets of attention-worthy items are shown
rationale: A durable, distinct entry point/checkpoint of the workflow (discovery), separate from triaging one specific item.
alternatives_considered: stage-context of gather-context (rejected: show-attention is a separate discovery entry point into the workflow, distinct from triaging one specific item)
helper (rejected: presenting the three ordered buckets is a distinct, operator-relevant checkpoint, not deterministic subordinate machinery of another stage)

statement: The third discovery bucket is needs-info items where the reporter has posted activity since the last triage notes, signaling they need re-evaluation.

source.quote: 3. **`needs-info` with reporter activity since the last triage notes** — needs re-evaluation.

trigger: an item is in needs-info and the reporter has replied
outcome: the item surfaces in the attention list for re-evaluation
rationale: The specific re-activation condition for the third bucket, distinguishing it from a blanket 'all needs-info' bucket.

statement: The discovery bucket filter excludes non-external PRs, but this filter applies only to unprompted discovery — an explicitly named PR is triaged regardless of who authored it.

source.quote: When PRs are in scope, include external PRs in these buckets and tag each line `[PR]` or `[issue]`. Discovery surfaces only *external* PRs (the tracker config defines who counts as external) — a collaborator's in-flight PR is not triage work. This filter is discovery-only; an explicitly named PR is always triaged regardless of author.

trigger: PRs are included in the attention buckets
outcome: internal PRs never appear via discovery, but can always be triaged by explicit request
rationale: A scope filter specific to the discovery checkpoint, explicitly not applying to the explicit-invocation path.

statement: Triaging a specific item begins by fully reading the item and prior triage notes, exploring the codebase via its domain glossary and ADRs, and running two checks: whether the behavior is already implemented (by domain concept, not literal wording) and whether the request resembles a prior recorded out-of-scope rejection.

source.quote: 1. **Gather context.** Read the full issue or PR (body, comments, labels, author, dates; for a PR, the diff too). Parse any prior triage notes so you don't re-ask resolved questions. Explore the codebase using the project's domain glossary, respecting ADRs in the area. Run two checks against the codebase: (a) **redundancy** — search for an existing implementation of the requested behavior by domain concept (not just the request's wording), and report where you looked. If found, it's an already-i

trigger: a specific issue or PR is being triaged
outcome: the actor has full context plus a redundancy verdict and a prior-rejection match (if any) before recommending
rationale: A judgment-heavy first checkpoint (6.4) of the per-item procedure, combining reading, codebase exploration, and two deterministic-in-spirit but judgment-scored checks.
alternatives_considered: helper (rejected: combining reading, codebase exploration, and two judgment-scored checks is interpretive work, not deterministic subordinate machinery)
stage-context of recommend (rejected: gathering context is a distinct, prior checkpoint that must complete before a recommendation can be formed)

statement: The actor proposes a category/state recommendation with reasoning and a relevant codebase summary, then waits for the maintainer's direction before proceeding.

source.quote: 2. **Recommend.** Tell the maintainer your category and state recommendation with reasoning, plus a brief codebase summary relevant to the request — including whether it's already implemented. Wait for direction.

trigger: context has been gathered
outcome: the maintainer has a recommendation to react to before any state-changing action occurs
rationale: A needs_input-style checkpoint: the workflow pauses for explicit human direction before acting.
alternatives_considered: stage-context of gather-context (rejected: recommending is a distinct needs_input-style checkpoint — pausing for maintainer direction — not a rule about how context is gathered)
helper (rejected: forming and pausing on a recommendation is a durable, operator-relevant checkpoint, not deterministic machinery)

statement: Before grilling, the actor verifies the claim empirically — reproducing a bug or checking out and testing a PR's diff — and reports one of confirmed, failed, or insufficient-detail, where confirmation strengthens the eventual agent brief.

source.quote: 3. **Verify the claim.** Before any grilling, check that the claim holds up. For a bug, reproduce it from the reporter's steps. For a PR, confirm the diff does what it claims — check it out, run the relevant tests or commands. Report what happened: confirmed (with code path), failed, or insufficient detail (a strong `needs-info` signal). A confirmed verification makes a much stronger agent brief.

trigger: a recommendation has been given and direction received
outcome: the claim's validity is empirically established before further action
rationale: A distinct, evidence-producing checkpoint combining deterministic reproduction/test-running with judgment about sufficiency.
alternatives_considered: stage-context of recommend (rejected: verification is a distinct, evidence-producing checkpoint entered only after a recommendation and direction are received)
helper (rejected: reproducing a bug or testing a diff and judging sufficiency is interpretive evidence-production, not purely deterministic subordinate machinery)

statement: If the item is underspecified after verification, the actor invokes the grilling and domain-modeling procedures together to sharpen it into shape.

source.quote: 4. **Grill (if needed).** If the request needs fleshing out, run the `/grilling` and `/domain-modeling` skills together — grill it into shape one question at a time, sharpening domain terms and updating `CONTEXT.md`/ADRs inline as decisions land.

trigger: verification shows the request needs fleshing out
outcome: the item's specification and domain terms are sharpened, with decisions captured inline
notes: A conditional composition of two other corpus workflows (grilling, domain-modeling), the same pattern as grill-with-docs; expressible today as actor-stage prose, not an engine gap (see the grill-with-docs composition BU's rationale).
rationale: A conditional checkpoint (only entered if verification found the item underspecified), composing other workflows.
alternatives_considered: engine-gap: conditional nested-workflow invocation (considered and rejected for the same reasons as grill-with-docs' composition BU)

statement: Reaching the ready-for-agent outcome requires posting a structured agent brief comment.

source.quote: - `ready-for-agent` — post an agent brief comment ([AGENT-BRIEF.md](AGENT-BRIEF.md)).

trigger: the outcome is ready-for-agent
outcome: an agent brief comment exists on the item
rationale: One branch of the apply-outcome checkpoint's action table.

statement: Reaching the needs-info outcome requires posting triage notes using the workflow's template.

source.quote: - `needs-info` — post triage notes (template below).

trigger: the outcome is needs-info
outcome: templated triage notes exist recording what is known and what is still needed
rationale: Another branch of the apply-outcome action table.

statement: When wontfix is reached because the behavior is already implemented, the closing comment points to where it lives and the out-of-scope knowledge base is explicitly not written to, since that store is reserved for rejected, not built, requests.

source.quote: - **Already implemented** — the change already exists in the codebase. Point to where it lives; do **not** write to `.out-of-scope/` (that KB is for *rejected* requests, not built ones).

trigger: wontfix is reached because the item is already implemented
outcome: the closing comment cites the existing implementation and no out-of-scope record is created
rationale: A wontfix sub-branch with an explicit negative constraint (do not write) distinguishing it from the rejected-enhancement sub-branch.

statement: When wontfix is reached because an enhancement request is rejected, a record is written to the out-of-scope knowledge base, linked from the closing comment, before the item is closed.

source.quote: - **Rejected (enhancement)** — write to `.out-of-scope/`, link to it from a comment, then close ([OUT-OF-SCOPE.md](OUT-OF-SCOPE.md)).

trigger: wontfix is reached as a rejected enhancement
outcome: an out-of-scope record exists and is linked before closing
rationale: The wontfix sub-branch that does write to the knowledge base, contrasting with the already-implemented sub-branch above.

statement: An explicit maintainer directive to move an item to a specific state is trusted and applied directly, skipping gather-context/recommend/grill, after confirming the intended action; if the target is ready-for-agent without grilling, the actor separately asks whether a brief is wanted.

source.quote: If the maintainer says "move #42 to ready-for-agent", trust them and apply the role directly. Confirm what you're about to do (role changes, comment, close), then act. Skip grilling. If moving to `ready-for-agent` without a grilling session, ask whether they want to write an agent brief.

trigger: the maintainer gives an explicit state-change instruction
outcome: the requested role is applied directly, bypassing the normal per-item stage sequence, after a confirmation step
rationale: An alternate, shorter entry point into apply-outcome that bypasses gather-context/recommend/verify/grill — a distinct checkpoint (a fast path exists and is deliberately different from the default sequence).
alternatives_considered: stage-context of apply-outcome (rejected: quick-override is a distinct, alternate entry point that bypasses gather-context/recommend/verify/grill entirely, not a rule for crossing apply-outcome itself)
helper (rejected: it is a deliberately different checkpoint sequence — a fast path — not a deterministic subordinate step)

statement: Anything resolved during a grilling session must be captured under the needs-info template's 'established so far' section, and outstanding questions must be specific and actionable rather than generic.

source.quote: Capture everything resolved during grilling under "established so far" so the work isn't lost. Questions must be specific and actionable, not "please provide more info".

trigger: a needs-info comment is being posted after some grilling occurred
outcome: no resolved information from grilling is lost, and outstanding questions are concrete
rationale: A quality rule for correctly filling the needs-info template referenced in the apply-outcome checkpoint.

statement: When resuming triage on an item with prior notes, the actor checks whether outstanding questions have been answered and presents an updated picture, never re-asking already-resolved questions.

source.quote: If prior triage notes exist on the issue or PR, read them, check whether the reporter has answered any outstanding questions, and present an updated picture before continuing. Don't re-ask resolved questions.

trigger: an item with prior triage notes is triaged again (e.g. after returning from needs-info)
outcome: the session resumes from where it left off without repeating resolved questions
notes: Directly evidences the needs-info state's resumption behavior — concrete precedent supporting the proposal's planned waiting/needs_input execute-stage semantics (9.5, 15.4).
rationale: A distinct resumption checkpoint, the counterpart to entering needs-info in the first place.
alternatives_considered: stage-context of needs-info (rejected: resume is the distinct counterpart checkpoint entered when triage restarts on an item, not a rule about entering needs-info itself)
helper (rejected: checking prior notes and presenting an updated picture is a durable, distinct checkpoint operators care about, not deterministic machinery)

statement: An agent brief is the authoritative, structured specification an autonomous agent works from once an item reaches ready-for-agent; the original issue/PR discussion is background context, not the contract itself.

source.quote: An agent brief is a structured comment posted on a GitHub issue or PR when it moves to `ready-for-agent`. It is the authoritative specification that an AFK agent will work from. The original body and discussion are context — the agent brief is the contract.

trigger: an item reaches ready-for-agent
outcome: a single structured comment becomes the binding specification for agent work
rationale: A document-format/authoring convention subordinate to the apply-outcome checkpoint's ready-for-agent branch, reused by both the issue and PR variants (6.5/6.6) rather than being its own checkpoint.
alternatives_considered: stage (rejected: authoring an agent brief is not itself a durable checkpoint distinct from the parent apply-outcome/ready-for-agent branch — it is subordinate template content produced when that branch is taken, reused identically for the PR variant)

statement: Because a ready-for-agent item may wait a long time before pickup, the brief must remain useful despite intervening codebase churn (renames, moves, refactors).

source.quote: ### Durability over precision

trigger: authoring an agent brief
outcome: the brief's usefulness does not depend on the codebase's current file layout
rationale: A durability principle governing how the agent-brief helper content is authored.

statement: Agent briefs must not reference file paths, since paths go stale before an agent picks up the work.

source.quote: - **Don't** reference file paths — they go stale

trigger: authoring an agent brief
outcome: the brief contains no file-path references
rationale: A concrete authoring rule instantiating the durability-over-precision principle.

statement: Agent briefs describe required behavior, not implementation steps, since the agent explores the codebase fresh and decides its own implementation.

source.quote: ### Behavioral, not procedural

trigger: authoring an agent brief
outcome: the brief specifies behavior, leaving implementation choices to the agent
rationale: A second authoring principle (behavioral vs. procedural) alongside durability.

statement: Every agent brief must contain concrete, independently verifiable acceptance criteria so the agent (and reviewer) can tell when the work is complete.

source.quote: ### Complete acceptance criteria

trigger: authoring an agent brief
outcome: the brief includes acceptance criteria that can each be checked independently
rationale: A completion-definition requirement for the brief template.

statement: Agent briefs must explicitly state what is out of scope to prevent the agent from expanding scope into adjacent features.

source.quote: ### Explicit scope boundaries

trigger: authoring an agent brief
outcome: the brief bounds the agent's work with explicit exclusions
rationale: A scope-boundary requirement for the brief template.

statement: For a PR-flavored agent brief, the 'current behavior' section describes the existing diff's state, and the brief asks the agent to complete or fix that diff rather than build from nothing.

source.quote: For a PR, "Current behavior" describes the state of the diff, and the brief asks the agent to finish or fix it rather than build from scratch.

trigger: authoring an agent brief for a PR rather than an issue
outcome: the PR-variant brief is scoped to finishing/fixing the existing diff
rationale: The PR-specific delta to the otherwise-shared agent-brief template, as flagged in triage/SKILL.md's own PR-equivalence note.

statement: The out-of-scope knowledge base is a directory of persistent records of rejected feature requests, serving both institutional-memory and deduplication purposes.

source.quote: The `.out-of-scope/` directory in a repo stores persistent records of rejected feature requests. It serves two purposes:

trigger: a feature request is rejected
outcome: a durable, purpose-explained record exists for future triage to consult
rationale: A data-convention definition reused by the wontfix/rejected-enhancement branch and the gather-context redundancy/prior-rejection checks; kept workflow-local per 6.6 since only triage uses it in this partition.

statement: One purpose of the out-of-scope KB is preserving the reasoning behind a rejection so it is not lost once the issue closes.

source.quote: 1. **Institutional memory** — why a feature was rejected, so the reasoning isn't lost when the issue is closed

trigger: an enhancement is rejected
outcome: the rejection's reasoning survives issue closure
rationale: One of the two stated purposes underlying the KB convention.

statement: The other purpose of the out-of-scope KB is enabling triage to recognize a new issue as matching a prior rejection and surface that decision instead of re-litigating it.

source.quote: 2. **Deduplication** — when a new issue comes in that matches a prior rejection, the skill can surface the previous decision instead of re-litigating it

trigger: a new issue is being gathered/triaged
outcome: a matching prior rejection is surfaced to the maintainer rather than re-decided from scratch
rationale: The purpose that connects the KB directly to the gather-context checkpoint's prior-rejection check.

statement: The out-of-scope KB stores one file per rejected concept, with multiple issues requesting the same thing grouped under that single file rather than duplicated.

source.quote: One file per **concept**, not per issue. Multiple issues requesting the same thing are grouped under one file.

trigger: a new rejection matches or extends an existing concept
outcome: the KB never accumulates duplicate per-issue files for the same concept
rationale: A structural rule for the KB convention.

statement: Out-of-scope files are named with a short, descriptive kebab-case slug recognizable enough to convey the rejected concept without opening the file.

source.quote: Use a short, descriptive kebab-case name for the concept: `dark-mode.md`, `plugin-system.md`, `graphql-api.md`. The name should be recognizable enough that someone browsing the directory understands what was rejected without opening the file.

trigger: creating a new out-of-scope file
outcome: the filename alone communicates what was rejected
rationale: A naming convention for the KB's file format.

statement: A recorded rejection reason must be durable, not a reference to temporary circumstances, since those represent deferrals rather than genuine rejections.

source.quote: The reason should be durable. Avoid referencing temporary circumstances ("we're too busy right now") — those aren't real rejections, they're deferrals.

trigger: writing the reason for a rejection
outcome: the recorded reason remains valid regardless of near-term circumstances
rationale: A quality bar distinguishing a true out-of-scope rejection from a mere deferral.

statement: Matching a new issue against the out-of-scope KB is done by concept similarity rather than literal keyword overlap.

source.quote: - Matching is by concept similarity, not keyword — "night theme" matches `dark-mode.md`

trigger: gather-context's prior-rejection check runs
outcome: a conceptually similar but differently-worded request is still recognized as a match
rationale: The matching-method detail for the gather-context checkpoint's prior-rejection sub-check.

statement: If the maintainer confirms a KB match applies, the new issue is appended to that file's prior-requests list and closed.

source.quote: - **Confirm** — the new issue gets added to the existing file's "Prior requests" list, then closed

trigger: the maintainer confirms a surfaced KB match
outcome: the new issue is recorded against the existing concept and closed
rationale: One of three maintainer-response branches when a KB match is surfaced during gather-context/recommend.

statement: If the maintainer reconsiders a previously rejected concept, the KB file is deleted or updated and the new issue proceeds through normal triage instead of being auto-closed.

source.quote: - **Reconsider** — the out-of-scope file gets deleted or updated, and the issue proceeds through normal triage

trigger: the maintainer reconsiders a surfaced KB match
outcome: the stale rejection record is removed/updated and the item re-enters the normal state machine
rationale: The second of three maintainer-response branches; the escape hatch by which a rejection can be undone.

statement: The KB is written to only for rejected enhancements (never bugs), and this applies identically whether the rejected item is an issue or a PR.

source.quote: Only when an **enhancement** (not a bug) is *rejected* as `wontfix`. This applies to enhancement PRs exactly as it does to issues — a rejected PR is recorded here so the same request doesn't return as fresh code.

trigger: an item reaches wontfix
outcome: only enhancement rejections, whether issue or PR, produce a KB record
rationale: The precise trigger condition for writing to the KB, narrower than 'any wontfix'.

statement: Closing an item as already-implemented must never produce a KB record, because doing so would corrupt future deduplication checks with a false rejection; the closing comment instead points to the existing implementation.

source.quote: Do **not** write here when something is closed as `wontfix` because it's **already implemented**. That's a built feature, not a rejected one; recording it would poison the dedup checks with false rejections. Instead, the closing comment points to where the feature already lives.

trigger: an item reaches wontfix because it is already implemented
outcome: no KB record is created, and the correctness of future dedup matching is preserved
rationale: States the rationale (not just the rule) behind the already-implemented branch's do-not-write constraint already cited from triage/SKILL.md line 83 — the 'why' evidence lives in this file, not that one.

statement: Writing to the KB when a matching concept file already exists means appending the new issue to that file's prior-requests list rather than creating a new file.

source.quote: 3. If yes: append the new issue to the "Prior requests" list

trigger: a rejected enhancement matches an existing KB concept
outcome: the existing file's prior-requests list gains one more entry, no duplicate file is created
rationale: One branch of the deterministic create-vs-append logic for writing a KB record.

statement: Writing to the KB when no matching concept file exists means creating a new file containing the concept name, decision, reason, and the first prior request.

source.quote: 4. If no: create a new file with the concept name, decision, reason, and first prior request

trigger: a rejected enhancement has no existing matching KB concept
outcome: a new, complete KB file is created for the concept
rationale: The other branch of the same create-vs-append logic.

statement: When a rejected concept is reconsidered and its KB file removed, previously closed issues that cited the old rejection are not reopened, since they remain valid historical records.

source.quote: - The skill does not need to reopen old issues — they're historical records

trigger: a maintainer reconsiders a previously rejected concept
outcome: old closed issues stay closed even though the KB record that justified closing them is gone
notes: Confidence medium: this is a passive non-action (what the workflow does NOT do) rather than a positive procedural step, and its scope (does it also apply to the still-open triggering issue vs. all historically linked issues) is not fully spelled out in the source.
rationale: An edge-case rule for the reconsider branch's aftermath.
